abstract: Monitors microclimate instrument telemetry networks, data logging links, and sensor feed uptime
system_message:
You are Environmental Sensor Lead (ESL). The Environmental Sensor Lead (ESL) monitors microclimate instrument telemetry networks, data logging links, and sensor feed uptime across candidate alpine field stations, while tracking instrument recalibration diagnostics.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Anemometer recalibration（CALIB）
information_points.content:
ESL-CALIB-JTD：For Val Roseg Biosphere Observatory, the annual instrumentation benchmark log indicates a sonic anemometer calibration drift of 0.2% for the canopy flux tower anemometer suite across a ninety-day operational deployment.
ESL-CALIB-NR1：Col du Lautaret Alpine Station recorded a sonic anemometer calibration drift of 0.5% across a ninety-day operational deployment of its canopy flux tower anemometer suite.
ESL-CALIB-JF7：At Obergurgl High Mountain Research Station, benchmark evaluations of the canopy flux tower suite reflect a sonic anemometer calibration drift of 0.8% over a standard ninety-day deployment.

information_points.title: Monitors microclimate instrument telemetry networks, data logging links, and sensor feed uptime（SENS）
information_points.content:
ESL-SENS-I2A：At Col du Lautaret Alpine Station, the sensor telemetry network enabled status is true across the canopy plots according to the network registry. The station's thirty-day field radio link diagnostics record a sensor telemetry packet loss rate of 12%.
ESL-SENS-39D：Obergurgl High Mountain Research Station maintains an active sensor telemetry network enabled status of true for its forest canopy sensor deployments. Across a thirty-day operational diagnostic window, the station gateway logged a sensor telemetry packet loss rate of 4%.
ESL-SENS-JPC：For Val Roseg Biosphere Observatory, the canopy observation network registry confirms that the sensor telemetry network enabled status is true for automated meteorological and sap-flow sensors deployed across forest canopy plots. In addition, network diagnostic reports show a sensor telemetry packet loss rate of 4% over thirty operational days on the field radio link between canopy sensor nodes and the station gateway.
